lines.japanese:
クリスマスイブを過ぎたクリスマスの日は、
基本的には、ただの冬の一日に過ぎなかった。
lines.english: Once Christmas Eve was over, Christmas Day was basically just another winter day.

lines.japanese:
明け方にやんでしまった雪は、
道行く人にただ寒さと歩きにくさを与えるだけで、
昼を過ぎた頃にはすっかり黒く土に溶け込んでいた。
lines.english: The snow had stopped before dawn, leaving the streets cold and treacherous underfoot. By early afternoon, it had melted into black slush and mud.

lines.japanese:
…そんな皮肉めいた見方しかできないのは、
自分の精神状態のせいという可能性も
否定できなかったけど。
lines.english: Maybe the state I was in was why I could see it only so cynically. I couldn’t rule that out.

lines.japanese:
そして、今はもうクリスマスでもない、
ただの冬の一日。
lines.english: And now Christmas itself was over. It was just another winter day.

lines.japanese: 部屋に帰り着いてから、２４時間以上が過ぎた。
lines.english: More than twenty-four hours had passed since I came home.

lines.japanese:
窓の外の黒い空が白く薄曇っていくのを
リアルタイムで全て視界に収め
明けない夜が本当にないということを痛感した。
lines.english: I watched the black sky beyond my window pale beneath a thin veil of cloud, minute by minute, and learned firsthand that no night lasts forever.

lines.japanese:
そして厚い雲に覆われた空は、
そのまままたリアルタイムで黒く染まっていき、
暮れない昼が本当にないということまで思い出させた。
lines.english: Then I watched that same cloud-heavy sky turn black again before my eyes, reminding me that no day lasts forever either.

lines.japanese:
それからは地獄の責め苦のように、
冬特有の長い夜を、灯りをつけないまま、
まんじりともせずに過ごし。
lines.english: Then came another long winter night, an infernal punishment I spent wide awake in the dark.

lines.japanese:
そして、やっと訪れた二度目の日の出は、
今度こそ明るい朝陽を俺の目に焼きつけた。
lines.english: When the second dawn finally came, the morning sun was bright enough to burn itself into my eyes.
lines.japaneseRuby:
そして、やっと訪れた二度目の日の出は、
今度こそ明るい[R朝陽^あさひ]を俺の目に焼きつけた。

lines.japanese:
そんなに時間が経過したというのに、
俺はまだ、あれから一睡もできてない。
lines.english: And through all of it, I still hadn't slept once.

lines.japanese:
疲れと眠気に苛まれているはずの頭は、
それでもただ一人の記憶を追い出すことができなくて、
割れんばかりの痛みばかりを俺にもたらす。
lines.english: My mind should have been buckling under the exhaustion, but it still couldn't drive out the memory of one person. All it could give me was pain enough to split my skull.

lines.japanese:
このまま部屋に一人で居続けたら、
頭がどうにかなってしまいそうだったけど…
lines.english: If I stayed alone in this room much longer, I felt like I was going to lose my mind…

lines.japanese:
結局、どこにも逃げ出す場所なんかなくて。
誰も逃げ場になってくれる人なんかいなくて。
lines.english: But there was nowhere I could run. No one I could run to.

lines.japanese: 俺はまだ、出口さえ見えない暗闇の中をさまよう。
lines.english: I was still wandering through a darkness with no exit in sight.

lines.japanese:
「ただ今留守にしております。
ご用の方は発信音の後にメッセージをお願いします」
lines.english: “No one is available to take your call. Please leave a message after the tone.”

lines.japanese: 「…本当に出かけてんのかよ？」
lines.english: “…Are you really out?”

lines.japanese:
「おい春希、この前の件だけどな、
帰ってきたらちゃんと話しようぜ？
…これ聞いたらすぐに連絡してくれ」
lines.english: “Haruki, listen. About what happened the other day—when you get back, we're going to talk, all right? Call me as soon as you hear this.”

lines.japanese:
「携帯とこっち、両方に入れとくから、
シカトすんじゃねえぞ？　じゃあな」
lines.english: “I’m leaving this on both your cell and your home phone, so don’t even think about ignoring me. Later.”

lines.japanese:
さっきの携帯も武也からだった。
これでもう、二日で九度目の居留守になる。
lines.english: The call to my cell just now had been Takeya too. That made nine times in two days I'd pretended not to be home.

lines.japanese:
最初は、いつまでも電話の通じない俺に対する
揶揄みたいな響きが含まれてた。
lines.english: At first, his voice had held a teasing edge, ribbing me for staying out so long.

lines.japanese:
それは、俺がまだ雪菜と一緒にいるんじゃないかって、
そんな下世話で温かい期待だったんだと思う。
lines.english: It was his dirty-minded but affectionate hope that I might still be with Setsuna.

lines.japanese:
けれど、昨日の夜中…
依緒からの連絡が来て以降、雲行きが怪しくなる。
lines.english: But then Io called late last night, and the mood changed.

lines.japanese:
彼女の口調は妙に切羽詰まってて、
けれど内容は、俺の予測を少しも外れはしなかった。
lines.english: There was a strange desperation in her voice, though what she told me was exactly what I'd expected.

lines.japanese: 雪菜と会ったこと。
lines.english: She had seen Setsuna.

lines.japanese:
何もなかったって雪菜が言ったこと。
笑ってたこと、泣いてなかったこと。
lines.english: Setsuna had told her nothing happened. She had smiled. She hadn't cried.

lines.japanese: …嘘を、ついてるってわかってしまったこと。
lines.english: And Io had known she was lying.

lines.japanese:
数年来の親友だからこそわかる些細な変化。
無理な明るさ、滲み出る虚しさ、隠せない痛み。
lines.english: The tiny differences only a friend of many years would notice: the forced brightness, the emptiness underneath, the pain she couldn't hide.

lines.japanese: それらの様々な負の感情が雪菜を蝕んでいるって。
lines.english: All of it was eating away at Setsuna.

lines.japanese:
…その電話があってから後、
朝まで、依緒と武也からのコールが
一時間おきくらいに数件続いてる。
lines.english: After that, Io and Takeya called every hour or so, right through the morning.

lines.japanese:
自分たちが仕掛人だからってだけじゃない。
純粋に俺たちを心配してるって口調から、
あいつらの焦燥感が伝わってくる。
lines.english: It wasn’t only because they had set the whole thing in motion. The strain in their voices made it obvious they were genuinely worried about us.

lines.japanese:
なのに俺は、
まるであいつらの慌てぶりを他人事のように俯瞰して、
スルーを繰り返す。
lines.english: And still I stood apart from their panic as if none of it had anything to do with me, letting call after call go unanswered.

lines.japanese:
だって、何と答えたらいいのかわからない。
近すぎるからこそ、何も話せない。
lines.english: Because I had no idea what I was supposed to tell them. They were too close. That was why I couldn't tell them anything.

lines.japanese: あいつらの反応がわかってるからこそ。
lines.english: Because I knew exactly how they'd react.

lines.japanese:
その反応が、俺にとって痛くて、
けれど俺を楽にしてしまうからこそ。
lines.english: Because their reaction would hurt—and in hurting me, it would make my life easier.

lines.japanese:
あいつらは、きっと俺に罰を与える。
怒り、嘆き、叱責して、必死に俺たちに干渉し、
なんとか解決策を探そうとするだろう。
lines.english: They would punish me. They'd rage at me, grieve over us, lecture me, throw themselves into our lives, and desperately search for a way to put things right.

lines.japanese:
そして俺は、そのあいつらの干渉に対して、
罰を受けた気になり、自らの思考を止めてしまう。
lines.english: And I would accept their interference as punishment enough, stop thinking for myself, and surrender my judgment to them.

lines.japanese:
そんな自己満足の停滞なんて意味がない。
解決していないのに、
解決した気になることほど最悪の事態はない。
lines.english: There was no point in that self-satisfied paralysis. Nothing could be worse than letting myself believe we'd solved something when we hadn't.

lines.japanese:
痛みを正面から受け止めたって、
先に進めないなら無駄だ。
lines.english: Even facing the pain head-on would mean nothing if I still couldn't move forward.

lines.japanese:
だって、俺が楽になった瞬間も、
雪菜にとっては何も解決してない、救われてない。
だったら俺一人が楽になることは、何ももたらさない。
lines.english: The moment I found relief, nothing would change for Setsuna. Nothing would be solved, and she would still be hurting. My relief alone would accomplish nothing.

lines.japanese: だから俺は…結局、動けない。
lines.english: And so… here I was, still unable to move.

lines.japanese:
この優しい陽射しに包まれた空が、
リアルタイムに赤く、そして黒く染まっていくのを
ただ眺める。
lines.english: I could only watch the sunlit sky turn red, then black, before my eyes.

lines.japanese:
次の夜が明けたら、
少しは前に進む気になれるんだろうかって…
lines.english: Wondering whether the next dawn might finally make me want to take even one step forward…

lines.japanese: そんな、初歩も初歩の自問自答を繰り返しつつ。
lines.english: Going around and around with a question so basic it was humiliating.
